OCPL Meeting Room Policies and Guidelines

The Obion County Public Library 
Meeting Room Policy and Procedure
Facilities and Meeting Space Use
1221 E. Reelfoot Ave. 
Union City, TN 38061
731-885-7000

The Reelfoot Bank meeting rooms of the Obion County Public Library are available for use by community groups for presentation of informational, cultural, educational, or civic meetings and programs in keeping with community standards and Library mission. These rooms have a square footage of 1,500sq ft total but can be split into two rooms for a square footage or 750sq ft each.  Each room can seat 50 guests. We ask that you please read over and observe the terms and conditions associated with the policy and procedures that the Obion County Public Library (hereafter referred to as OCPL) are set forth. If you have any questions regarding the outlined information, please do not hesitate to ask. The library does not advocate or endorse the viewpoints of any group or individual.

I. RESERVATION POLICY
Events sponsored by OCPL, the Friends of the Library and other agencies of Obion County or Union City governments have first priority for use of the meeting rooms. Thereafter, requests will be considered in the following order: 
Community non-profit, cultural, or civic organizations
Organizations whose primary purpose is for-profit
Business use for meeting or educational purposes
Businesses may not sell products nor charge for services rendered
Each organization must fill out a reservation application form either in person or the OCPL web-site. Reoccurring reservations will be accepted for up to six months and must then be renewed. A call of inquiry of availability does not constitute a room reservation. Requests will be considered on a first come, first served basis. 
Groups must list a contact person that can be contacted for questions; whether questions arise of OCPL staff or public interest in a public meeting.

II. CANCELLATION POLICY
Groups should notify the library as soon as possible if a meeting is canceled. Groups with two “no call/no shows” in a calendar year will not be permitted further reservations for one year. 
III. FEES FOR USAGE
Fees for businesses and for-profit organizations:
Study Room:
                          $25.00
Half room:
Half day (less than four hours) $25.00
Whole day (over four hours) $50.00
Full room:
Half day (less than four hours) $50.00
Whole day (over four hours) $100.00
Fees for individuals for birthday parties, showers, receptions, etc.:
 $50.00
At this time weddings can not be held at the OCPL.
IV. SETUP UP, USE, AND TAKE DOWN
Groups are responsible for setting up the room(s) and should include time for set up and take down into their reservation time. Food and drink may be served within the meeting room(s). Groups are allowed to use the kitchenette area located in the hallway. Food for the occasion may be stored in the kitchenette refrigerator the day before the event. Groups are responsible for following food safety guidelines. The room(s) must be left in the same condition as they are found. 
Meeting Conclusion Checklist:
Floor is cleared of any debris. A small carpet sweeper is located in the hallway beside the coat rack for your convenience 
Tables are wiped down and cleaned 
All decorations have been removed
Lights have been turned off 
Tables and chairs have been replaced in the same order as arrived
Kitchenette has been cleaned and all food and drink removed. 
A cleaning basket is available inside the kitchenette for your convenience with meeting clean up
OCPL reserves the right to charge the contact person listed for the reservation double the rental rate, i.e rental rate is $50.00 cleaning charge would be $100.00, for improper conditions being left. Groups may not store or leave equipment, supplies, decorations, or personal belongings in the library. OCPL is not responsible for lost, damaged, or stolen items. 
V.TIMES FOR USE
Meetings must begin while the library is open. If meetings are held after library hours the event must end by nine o’clock in the evening (9:00p.m). This includes all persons and clean up. Meetings occurring during this time will only have access to the hallway bathrooms, there will be no access to the rest of the library. No reservations can be made for Sundays or holidays observed by the library. Meetings can not interfere with OCPL operations. The sound system may be used but sound must be confined to the meeting room space. 
OCPL Hours: 
Monday 9:00am - 7:30p.m
Tuesday 9:00am - 7:30p.m
Wednesday 9:00am - 6:00pm
Thursday 9:00am - 7:30p.m
Friday 9:00a.m - 5:00pm
Saturday 9:00am - 3:30pm
Hours are subject to change and will be posted on library property as well as social media. If OCPL must close due to an emergency or weather related event every effort will be made to notify the group(s) scheduled to the meeting room(s). During adverse weather group contact persons should monitor OCPLs Facebook page for unscheduled closings.  
VI.AUDIOVISUAL
OCPL will provide audiovisual equipment as indicated on the reservation form. The group is responsible for indicating any equipment needed. OCPL is not responsible for setup or the operation of audiovisual equipment.
VII. DECORATIONS 
Decorations for your event are welcome; however, we ask that you please note the following rules: 

 Do not attach any decorations to the painted walls, ceiling tiles, glass surfaces, and any      other finished surface. Tacking strips are available in each room for posting materials and decorations 
Decorations must be removed immediately after the event
OCPL will not be held responsible for any items remaining after an event
Lighted candles are not allowed; in replacement flameless or battery operated candles may be used. 
VIII. PUBLICITY
OCPL does not advocate or endorse the viewpoints of any group or individual. Meeting room use shall not be published in such a way as to imply library sponsorship. All printed materials such as flyers or posters publicizing meetings at the library must contain the following disclaimer: “Use of the library meeting space does not constitute an endorsement of the program/meeting of its content by The Obion County Public Library.” 
IX. ALCOHOL & DRUGS POSSESSING 
Alcoholic beverages in an open container, or consuming or selling any alcoholic beverage while on OCPL property is strictly PROHIBITED AT ALL TIMES. The use of illegal drugs, alcohol, and gambling are prohibited on or in any OCPL facilities.

X. SMOKING POLICY 

Smoking is strictly prohibited on and in all OCPL facilities. 
XI. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT
Those planning to use the meeting room(s) must sign the statement below accepting responsibility for damage or loss of library equipment and furnishings. The person who signs the statement is responsible for the conduct of the group. Failure to abide by the library’s meeting room policies and procedure may result in fine and/or the cancellation or refusal of future reservations.

Obion County Public Library
Park Policy

Purpose: 
The grounds of the Obion County Public Library are available for use by community groups for presentation of informational, cultural, educational, civic meetings or programs. It is also available for individual’s personal use, such as walking, reading, picnicking or enjoyment. 

Policy: 
Events sponsored by the Obion County Public Library, the Friends of the Library and other agencies of Obion County or Union City governments have first priority for use of the park. 
Thereafter, requests will be considered in the following order:
•	Community non-profit, cultural or civic organizations
•	Organizations whose primary purpose if non-profit.
•	Business or individual use for meeting or educational purposes

No businesses or individuals may use the park for profit or charge for services. 

Businesses may use the library grounds for not-for- profit activities. Programs involving the sale, advertisement or promotion of commercial products or the solicitation for the future sale of commercial products, are prohibited.

Fundraising events or solicitation of any kind are not permitted unless sponsored by the Friends of the Library. 

The library does not advocate or endorse the viewpoints of any group or individual. Park usage shall not be publicized in such a way as to imply library sponsorship. 

Reservation Policy:

Each group must fill out a reservation application form. Recurring reservations will be accepted for up to six months and must then be renewed. A call of inquiry of availability does not constitute a park reservation.

Requests will be considered on a first come, first serve basis. 

All use of library grounds is subject of the approval of the library board.

Groups planning to use the park must sign a statement accepting responsibility for damage to the park or library equipment. The person who signs the statement is responsible for the conduct of the group.

Failure to abide by the park policy and guidelines may result in the cancellation for refusal of future reservations. 

Guidelines:
Any program or activity held in the park must not interfere with library operations. 

Groups or individuals, who use the park must leave the grounds in good order, the library reserves the right to charge a fee if additional maintenance is required. 

If the park is to be used after hours, the side gate will be unlocked for entrance or exit.

Visitors may use the park at their own risk. The library is not responsible for lost or stolen items. 

Children may not be left unattended in the park or on any library property. 

Picnics are allowed in the park but patrons must pick up all trash and leave the premises in good order. Trashcans are available on the patio. 

The patio may be used by groups or individuals for casual meetings. 

Bicycles, skates, skate boards or any recreational vehicles are not allowed in the park. 

Playing in the fountain is prohibited.

** Please note that the Park is a public space and will not be closed for patron events. The Park can only be used during standard business operating hours.**
